data.name: Qahtan
data.gender_notes: Qahtan is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.short_meaning: Owner of the plain, fertile lands
data.long_meaning: A person who possesses and manages fertile lands, who is generous and provides for his people. The name Qahtan carries the meaning “Owner of the plain, fertile lands” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic. Parents who choose Qahtan usually hope their child will grow to embody owner of the plain, fertile lands and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes abundance, prosperity, and generosity, representing a spiritual leader who provides for his community
data.etymology: Qahtan belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Owner of the plain, fertile lands.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Qahtan total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

data.cultural_impact: The name Qahtan is believed to have originated from the ancient civilization of Sheba, mentioned in the Quran and the Bible, located in present-day Yemen. Qahtan is recognized in Islamic culture as a name of a great and generous king, who ruled the land of Yemen with wisdom and prosperity, providing for his people and ensuring their wellbeing.
data.spiritual_significance: In Islamic spirituality, the name Qahtan signifies the concept of abundance, generosity, and provision. Qahtan represents the idea of a leader who cultivates the land not only for material wealth, but also for the spiritual growth and prosperity of his people. The name serves as a reminder to strive towards being a provider, not just for our material needs, but for our spiritual ones as well. It encourages us to be generous with our time, energy, and resources, not just for ourselves, but for the benefit of the greater community. Moreover, the name Qahtan reflects the belief that leaders, like Prophets, are not just human beings but vessels of Allah's mercy and blessings upon their peoples.
